passages.text: These are the words of King Lemuel—the burden that his mother taught him: What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
passages.sermon:
King Lemuel spoke these words.
He was a king.
His mother taught him these things.
She gave him a message that was important.
She said, “What can I say to you, my son?”
She called him her son.
She said he was the son from her own womb.
She said he was the son she promised to God in her vows.”
passages.original: דִּ֭בְרֵי לְמוּאֵ֣ל מֶ֑לֶךְ מַ֝שָּׂ֗א אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ יִסְּרַ֥תּוּ אִמּֽוֹ׃ מַה־ בְּ֭רִי וּמַֽה־ בַּר־ בִּטְנִ֑י וּ֝מֶה בַּר־ נְדָרָֽי׃

passages.text: Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings.
passages.sermon:
King Lemuel’s mother spoke to him.
She gave him wise advice.
She said, “Do not give your strength to women.
Do not give your ways to those who destroy kings.”
passages.original: אַל־ תִּתֵּ֣ן לַנָּשִׁ֣ים חֵילֶ֑ךָ וּ֝דְרָכֶ֗יךָ לַֽמְח֥וֹת מְלָכִֽין׃

passages.text: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink, lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice.
passages.sermon:
King Lemuel received teachings from his mother.
She spoke to him as a king.
She said, “Kings must not drink wine.
Kings must not desire strong drink.
Rulers must not crave strong drink.
If a king drinks wine, he may forget the law.
If a ruler drinks strong drink, he may forget what is right.
A king who forgets the law may deny justice.
He may deprive oppressed people of justice.”
passages.original: אַ֤ל לַֽמְלָכִ֨ים׀ לְֽמוֹאֵ֗ל אַ֣ל לַֽמְלָכִ֣ים שְׁתוֹ־ יָ֑יִן וּ֝לְרוֹזְנִ֗ים אוֹ שֵׁכָֽר׃ פֶּן־ יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח מְחֻקָּ֑ק וִֽ֝ישַׁנֶּה דִּ֣ין כָּל־ בְּנֵי־ עֹֽנִי׃

passages.text: Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives advice to rulers and leaders.
It tells them how to act with wisdom and justice.
It says, “Give strong drink to the one who is perishing.”
It also says, “Give wine to the person who is bitter in soul.”
The passage means to give comfort to those who suffer or are in distress.
passages.original: תְּנוּ־ שֵׁכָ֣ר לְאוֹבֵ֑ד וְ֝יַיִן לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
passages.sermon:
A man is perishing.
He is bitter in soul.
Let him drink.
He will forget his poverty.
He will not remember his misery anymore.
passages.original: יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח רִישׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲמָל֗וֹ לֹ֣א יִזְכָּר־ עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.
passages.sermon:
Speak up for people who cannot speak for themselves.
Defend the rights of all who are helpless.
Support those who have no power.
Stand for everyone who is dispossessed.
passages.original: פְּתַח־ פִּ֥יךָ לְאִלֵּ֑ם אֶל־ דִּ֝֗ין כָּל־ בְּנֵ֥י חֲלֽוֹף׃

passages.text: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy.
passages.sermon:
Speak up for others.
Judge with fairness.
Defend the rights of the poor.
Defend the rights of the needy.
passages.original: פְּתַח־ פִּ֥יךָ שְׁפָט־ צֶ֑דֶק וְ֝דִ֗ין עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃פ

passages.text: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
passages.sermon:
A wife of noble character is rare.
She is hard to find.
She has great worth.
She is more precious than rubies.
passages.original: אֵֽשֶׁת־ חַ֭יִל מִ֣י יִמְצָ֑א וְרָחֹ֖ק מִפְּנִינִ֣ים מִכְרָֽהּ׃

passages.text: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.
passages.sermon:
A wife of noble character is trustworthy.
Her husband trusts her completely.
He does not lack anything valuable.
She provides for him faithfully.
passages.original: בָּ֣טַח בָּ֭הּ לֵ֣ב בַּעְלָ֑הּ וְ֝שָׁלָ֗ל לֹ֣א יֶחְסָֽר׃

passages.text: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.
passages.sermon:
A wife of noble character acts with goodness.
She does not do harm to her husband.
She brings good to her husband every day of her life.
She never brings harm to him at any time in her life.
passages.original: גְּמָלַ֣תְהוּ ט֣וֹב וְלֹא־ רָ֑ע כֹּ֝֗ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּֽיה׃

passages.text: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a virtuous wife.
She chooses wool.
She chooses flax.
She works with her hands.
She works eagerly.
passages.original: דָּ֭רְשָׁה צֶ֣מֶר וּפִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַ֝תַּ֗עַשׂ בְּחֵ֣פֶץ כַּפֶּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.
passages.sermon:
This woman is wise and diligent.
\r\nShe is like merchant ships.
\r\nShe brings her food from far away places.
\r\nShe works hard to provide for her household.
passages.original: הָ֭יְתָה כָּאֳנִיּ֣וֹת סוֹחֵ֑ר מִ֝מֶּרְחָ֗ק תָּבִ֥יא לַחְמָֽהּ׃

passages.text: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants.
passages.sermon:
This woman is diligent and caring.
She gets up while it is still night.
She provides food for her household.
She gives portions to her maidservants.
passages.original: וַתָּ֤קָם׀ בְּע֬וֹד לַ֗יְלָה וַתִּתֵּ֣ן טֶ֣רֶף לְבֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝חֹ֗ק לְנַעֲרֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a wise and diligent woman.
She examines a field.
She decides to buy the field.
She uses her own earnings.
She plants a vineyard with what she has earned.
passages.original: זָמְמָ֣ה שָׂ֭דֶה וַתִּקָּחֵ֑הוּ מִפְּרִ֥י כַ֝פֶּ֗יהָ נְטַע כָּֽרֶם׃

passages.text: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.
passages.sermon:
This verse describes a virtuous woman.
She prepares herself with strength.
She makes her waist strong.
She shows that her arms are strong.
passages.original: חָֽגְרָ֣ה בְע֣וֹז מָתְנֶ֑יהָ וַ֝תְּאַמֵּ֗ץ זְרֹעוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
passages.sermon:
This woman works hard and manages her business well.
She sees that her profit is good.
She keeps her lamp burning at night.
She does not let her lamp go out.
She stays diligent and alert even when it is dark.
passages.original: טָ֭עֲמָה כִּי־ ט֣וֹב סַחְרָ֑הּ לֹֽא־ יִכְבֶּ֖ה בַלַּיִל נֵרָֽהּ׃

passages.text: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a virtuous woman.
She works with her hands.
She reaches out her hands to the distaff.
She holds the spindle with her fingers.
passages.original: יָ֭דֶיהָ שִׁלְּחָ֣ה בַכִּישׁ֑וֹר וְ֝כַפֶּ֗יהָ תָּ֣מְכוּ פָֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
passages.sermon:
This woman acts with kindness and generosity.
She opens her arms to the poor.
She reaches out her hands to the needy.
She helps those who lack what they need.
passages.original: כַּ֭פָּהּ פָּרְשָׂ֣ה לֶעָנִ֑י וְ֝יָדֶ֗יהָ שִׁלְּחָ֥ה לָֽאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
passages.sermon:
This woman cares for her family.
She does not fear when snow comes.
Her family is safe from the cold.
Everyone in her house wears warm, scarlet clothes.
passages.original: לֹא־ תִירָ֣א לְבֵיתָ֣הּ מִשָּׁ֑לֶג כִּ֥י כָל־ בֵּ֝יתָ֗הּ לָבֻ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
passages.sermon:
This woman is wise and diligent.
She makes coverings for her bed.
She wears fine linen.
She wears purple clothing.
passages.original: מַרְבַדִּ֥ים עָֽשְׂתָה־ לָּ֑הּ שֵׁ֖שׁ וְאַרְגָּמָ֣ן לְבוּשָֽׁהּ׃

passages.text: Her husband is known at the city gate, where he sits among the elders of the land.
passages.sermon:
Her husband is well known.
People recognize him at the city gate.
He sits there with the elders of the land.
passages.original: נוֹדָ֣ע בַּשְּׁעָרִ֣ים בַּעְלָ֑הּ בְּ֝שִׁבְתּ֗וֹ עִם־ זִקְנֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.
passages.sermon:
A wise and industrious woman makes linen garments.
She sells these garments.
She also makes sashes.
She gives the sashes to merchants.
passages.original: סָדִ֣ין עָ֭שְׂתָה וַתִּמְכֹּ֑ר וַ֝חֲג֗וֹר נָתְנָ֥ה לַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽי׃

passages.text: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
passages.sermon:
This woman is strong.
She is honorable.
Strength covers her like clothing.
Honor covers her like clothing.
She looks to the future without fear.
She laughs at the days to come.
passages.original: עֹז־ וְהָדָ֥ר לְבוּשָׁ֑הּ וַ֝תִּשְׂחַ֗ק לְי֣וֹם אַחֲרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
passages.sermon:
This woman speaks with wisdom.
She opens her mouth and gives wise words.
She teaches kindness.
Her tongue gives faithful instruction.
She always speaks with care and understanding.
She uses her words to help and guide others.
passages.original: פִּ֭יהָ פָּתְחָ֣ה בְחָכְמָ֑ה וְתֽוֹרַת־ חֶ֝֗סֶד עַל־ לְשׁוֹנָֽהּ׃

passages.text: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
passages.sermon:
This woman manages her household.
She pays close attention to everything that happens in her home.
She does not live in laziness.
She does not take part in idleness.
She stays active and diligent.
passages.original: צ֭וֹפִיָּה הֲלִיכ֣וֹת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְלֶ֥חֶם עַ֝צְל֗וּת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵֽל׃

passages.text: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a noble woman.
\r\nHer children stand up.
\r\nHer children call her blessed.
\r\nHer husband also praises her.
\r\nHe says, “Many daughters have done noble things.”
\r\nHe says, “But you surpass them all.”
passages.original: קָ֣מוּ בָ֭נֶיהָ וַֽיְאַשְּׁר֑וּהָ בַּ֝עְלָ֗הּ וַֽיְהַֽלְלָהּ׃ רַבּ֣וֹת בָּ֭נוֹת עָ֣שׂוּ חָ֑יִל וְ֝אַ֗תְּ עָלִ֥ית עַל־ כֻּלָּֽנָה׃

passages.text: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
passages.sermon:
Charm can deceive people.
Beauty does not last.
A woman who fears the LORD deserves praise.
People should honor a woman who respects God.
passages.original: שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭חֵן וְהֶ֣בֶל הַיֹּ֑פִי אִשָּׁ֥ה יִרְאַת־ יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תִתְהַלָּֽל׃

passages.text: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
passages.sermon:
A woman who fears the LORD deserves honor.
Give her what she has earned.
Let her enjoy the results of her hard work.
Let people praise her deeds in public places.
Let her works bring her praise at the city gates.
passages.original: תְּנוּ־ לָ֭הּ מִפְּרִ֣י יָדֶ֑יהָ וִֽיהַלְל֖וּהָ בַשְּׁעָרִ֣ים מַעֲשֶֽׂיהָ׃
